draft.title: Spartiates, perioikoi and helots
card: Spartiates
The full citizens of Sparta. They trained as soldiers and were expected to serve the state in the army.
Perioikoi
Free people who lived in nearby towns but were not citizens. They traded, made goods and worked as craftworkers.
Helots
Serfs owned by the state, not by one master. They farmed the land and produced the food that supported the Spartiates.
Spartiates held political rights and did not farm or trade. Perioikoi were free but had no say in citizen affairs. Helots were not free.
draft.remember: Spartiates fought, perioikoi traded and made goods, and helots farmed.

a.q: Which group in Spartan society was free but not a full citizen?
a.why: The perioikoi were free people who lived in nearby towns but did not have citizen rights. The Spartiates were full citizens, so they are the tempting wrong answer. The helots were not free.
a.clue: Look for the group that was free but had no citizen rights.

b.q: Kallias is a Spartan who farms land by the Eurotas but belongs to no private owner. The state controls him and he is not free. Which group does he belong to?
b.why: Farming land for the state, with no freedom, describes the helots. The perioikoi are the tempting wrong answer because they also worked, but they were free and traded or made goods. The Spartiates were citizen soldiers.
b.clue: Which group was owned by the state and worked the land?

problems.detail: The question calls Kallias 'a Spartan'. That can suggest a Spartiate (citizen), which clashes with him being an unfree helot. Better: 'Kallias lives in Laconia and farms land by the Eurotas…'.

check.summary: The facts and the intended answers are right. In question b, calling the helot Kallias 'a Spartan' could confuse students, because the word suggests a citizen.

proposal.title: Spartiates, perioikoi and helots
card: Spartiates
The full citizens of Sparta. They trained as soldiers and were expected to serve the state in the army.
Perioikoi
Free people who lived in nearby towns but were not citizens. They traded, made goods and worked as craftworkers.
Helots
Serfs, people tied to the land, owned by the state rather than by one master. They farmed the land and produced the food that supported the Spartiates.
Spartiates held political rights and did not farm or trade. Perioikoi were free but had no say in citizen affairs. Helots were not free.
proposal.remember: Spartiates fought, perioikoi traded and made goods, and helots farmed.

a.q: What set the perioikoi apart from the helots?
opts: The perioikoi were free but had no citizen rights
The perioikoi held full citizen rights in Sparta
The perioikoi were serfs owned by the Spartan state
The perioikoi farmed the land to feed the Spartiates
a.why: The perioikoi were free, while the helots were not, yet the perioikoi still lacked citizen rights. Saying they held full citizen rights is the tempting wrong answer, but that describes the Spartiates. Being state-owned serfs who farmed describes the helots.
a.clue: Think about freedom and citizen rights separately.

b.q: Kallias lives in Laconia and farms land by the Eurotas. He belongs to no private owner, but the state controls him and he is not free. Which group is he part of?
b.why: Farming the land while owned by the state and not free describes the helots. Privately owned slaves is tempting because Kallias is not free, but helots belonged to the state, not to one master. The perioikoi were free and traded or made goods.
b.clue: Who owns Kallias, and does he farm?

a.best: The perioikoi were free but had no citizen rights
